name: FL Studio
tagline: A full digital audio workstation for producing, mixing and mastering music, built around a pattern sequencer and piano roll.

pricing.basis: one-time perpetual license with free lifetime updates
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Editions are a one-time purchase, not a subscription, so a monthly figure is misleading.

verdictSummary: An agent can absolutely give you a working step sequencer with samples, a piano roll and a WAV export in an afternoon, and that is genuinely fun. It is not a DAW. FL Studio is a real-time low-latency audio engine, a VST/VST3 plugin host, a mixer with sends and automation, dozens of shipped synths and effects, and a project format that a decade of your unfinished songs already live in. The gap is not features you forgot, it is thousands of hours of DSP and plugin-host edge cases, plus everything third-party you bought that only loads inside a real host. The honest move is a toy sequencer for sketching ideas and keeping the license.
coreLoopDIY: A local browser app that sequences your own samples on a step grid, plays a simple synth line from a piano roll, and renders the loop to a WAV file.
requirements: Node 20+ and a modern Chromium browser for Web Audio and Web MIDI
Your own sample files, drums and one-shots, in a local folder
A machine quiet enough that browser audio latency does not ruin your day
whatYouLose: VST/VST3/AU plugin hosting, so every instrument and effect you already own is unusable
The bundled instruments and effects: Sytrus, Harmor, Serum-class synths, the whole stock effect rack
A real mixer: buses, sends, sidechaining, per-track automation, latency compensation
Reliable low-latency monitoring while recording, which the browser audio stack will not give you
Project portability: nobody else can open your format, and you cannot open your old .flp files
moatNotes: The plugin ecosystem is the real lock: a host that cannot load VSTs is not competing with a host that can.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a DAW is one of the few remaining categories where the software genuinely is the product, and a one-time license with lifetime updates prices in at less than a couple of months of most SaaS. People pay for a stable audio engine that does not glitch during a take, for stock instruments that sound finished, and for the ability to load the plugins they already own. The switching cost is also brutal in the mundane way: your muscle memory, your templates and your half-finished projects all live in one format.
notes: A step sequencer is a weekend; an audio engine is not. The moat is twenty-plus years of DSP and plugin-host compatibility, plus every third-party VST you already bought.
prompt:
Build a local browser-based loop sketchpad called "Sketchpad". This is a toy music sequencer, not a DAW. Be honest about scope.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Vite + TypeScript, vanilla DOM, no framework.
- Web Audio API directly, no Tone.js or other audio library.
- No backend, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud. Everything runs from `npm run dev`.
- Persist project state to localStorage plus explicit JSON export/import.

Features, in scope:
- Load samples from a local folder the user picks via a file input; decode to AudioBuffers and show them as pads.
- A 16-step, 8-track drum grid. Per-step on/off, per-track volume and pan, per-step velocity via right-click cycling.
- One monophonic synth track: a small piano roll, 2 octaves, 16 steps, sawtooth or square oscillator into a lowpass filter with ADSR envelope.
- Transport: play, stop, loop, BPM 60-200, swing amount. Schedule with a lookahead scheduler using AudioContext.currentTime, not setInterval-per-note.
- Master bus: gain, a simple soft-clip limiter, and one shared feedback-delay send.
- Render the loop offline to a WAV file via OfflineAudioContext and trigger a download. Write the WAV encoder yourself, 16-bit PCM.
- Optional Web MIDI input: map incoming note-on to the synth track if a device is present, degrade silently if not.

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt:
- VST/AU plugin hosting, audio recording from a microphone, multitrack arrangement beyond a single 16-step loop, time stretching, notation, mobile support.

Deliverables: working app, a README that states plainly what this is not, and a `samples/` folder with a note telling the user to drop their own files in.
No API keys are needed. If you add any config, read it from .env and commit a .env.example.
